points.label: Divine response
points.left: God’s sons present themselves. Satan speaks. Job is commended. Motives are disputed. The LORD allows Satan to act but sets a limit.
points.right: Joshua, Satan, the LORD’s angel, filthy garments, cleansing, charge, and promised access form a court-like vision.

payload.posture: Read both WEBU passages side by side. Keep each passage’s actors, setting, order, and identity claims distinct.

rightEvidence.title: Satan opposes the high priest before rebuke and cleansing

payload.tension: Satan stands before the LORD in both scenes. One allows testing. The other ends in rebuke and restoration.
payload.title: Accusation before the LORD in Job and Zechariah
